question: Let $P,Q,R,S$ and $T$ be statements such that if $P$ is true then both $Q$ and $S$ are true, and if both $R$ and $S$ are true then $T$ is false. Then we have:

options.A: If $T$ is true then both $P$ and $R$ must be true.
options.B: If $T$ is true then $P$ and $R must be false.
options.C: If $T$ is true then at least one of $P$ and $R$ must be true.
options.D: If $T$ is true then at least one of $P$ and $R$ must be false.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
